 Over 12,100 Myanmar nationals repatriated this year, says Home Ministry
 By RAGANANTHINI VETHASALAM  and  DIVYA THERESA RAVI 
 Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026
 | 9:34 AM MYT

 KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 12,176 Myanmar nationals were repatriated from Malaysia in the first 10 months of 2026, according to the Home Ministry.
 In a parliamentary written reply dated Monday (Nov 16), the ministry said the figure includes 1,476 detainees who were sent back on Sept 29 during a large-scale repatriation operation aboard a Myanmar Navy vessel.
 However, the ministry clarified that repatriation statistics are recorded based on nationality verified by the country of origin rather than ethnicity, meaning the figures do not specifically reflect the number of Rohingya individuals sent back.
 Meanwhile, Immigration Department records as of Oct 31 showed that 11,208 Myanmar nationals were being held at immigration detention depots nationwide, including 6,294 Rohingya individuals. Separately, data from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) recorded 133,400 Rohingya refugees and asylum seekers registered in Malaysia as of Sept 30.
 The ministry noted that deporting undocumented foreign nationals requires close cooperation from their home countries to verify nationalities and issue travel documents.
 "In this regard, the Home Ministry continues to work closely with the National Security Council (NSC) and Foreign Ministry in conducting negotiations and coordinating with the Myanmar government, particularly to expedite nationality verification, the issuance of travel documents, and the acceptance of Myanmar nationals back into their country of origin," it said.
 Addressing how undocumented migrants enter the country, the ministry said regional migrant smuggling syndicates use ungazetted sea routes to move individuals from Myanmar or Bangladesh, often via transit countries, into Malaysia.
 It added that specific entry routes can only be determined through enforcement investigations and record checks, noting that border security is a shared responsibility across multiple security and enforcement agencies within their respective jurisdictions.
 The reply was in response to Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong), who asked for the latest number of Rohingya refugees in Malaysia, how many were repatriated this year, how they entered the country, and which agencies were responsible for border security lapses.
